notes: §1985:XII.2.3 SR1: 'If more than one COBOL library is available during compilation, text-name-1 must be qualified by library-name-1 identifying the COBOL library in which the text associated with text-name-1 resides. Within one COBOL library, each text-name must be unique.' The second sentence holds: CopyProcessor#LocateInLibrary takes the first file of the name and suffix list, so a text-name names one text in a library (DOC-A.1-40). The first is not implemented at any edition: CopyProcessor#FindCopybook resolves an unqualified COPY against the default library (LibraryPlaces) even when a named library (a subdirectory of a place, which OF/IN reaches) is available, and nothing at --std 85 counts libraries or refuses the unqualified form. Probes at 85 (cwd holding MSGTXT.cpy and LIBB/MSGTXT.cpy): COPY MSGTXT. COPY MSGTXT OF LIBB. COPY MSGTXT IN LIBB. compiles and prints DEFAULT TEXT / LIBB TEXT / LIBB TEXT, rc 0; an unqualified COPY of a text only LIBC holds is CBL3620 (no fallback); literal forms refused COBOL0900. The witness has one library and passes. kb/Work PB5473 holds the defect (code read: coderead-85/out-read4/rd-03.json).

next.reason: 'Within one COBOL library, each text-name must be unique' is kept by §2023:7.2.3.3 SR3, and library-name-1 still identifies the library holding the text (§2023:7.2.3.4 GR2). But 1985 requires text-name-1 to be qualified by library-name-1 whenever more than one library is available; 2023 has no such rule: 'When neither library-name-1 nor literal-2 is specified, a default COBOL library is used' (§2023:7.2.3.4 GR3). An unqualified COPY that 1985 refused with several libraries is accepted in 2023. Looser.
